title: finding(components/plugin-list): the `list` registration's authoring input recommends `items[].body` — a key the published `ListItem` face refuses and `ListItemSchema` silently strips, while the renderer really reads it
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (`session_01XeoGH6X7MtfbjcRDscyXi1`) from the `out_of_scope_findings` of the objectui#9256 dev report (`5691855092`). ⛔ Not repaired there: the file is a registration site outside that card's declared surface, and family D's ruling is node-level while this defect is item-level.

⛔ No `domain:*`, no `type`, no `priority:*` on this card — grading and routing are the triage seat's, and this seat does not produce them.

## What is wrong

`packages/components/src/renderers/data-display/list.tsx` registers `list` with an **authoring input** whose description reads, in substance, *"Array of strings or objects with content/body"* — pointing an author, the designer UI, or an AI at `items[].body`.

Three faces disagree about that key:

| face | what it does with `items[].body` |
|:--|:--|
| the **registration's own authoring input** | recommends it by name |
| the published `ListItem` TypeScript face | does ⛔ **not** declare it — authoring it is an excess-property error |
| `ListItemSchema` (zod) | **silently strips** it — a plain `z.object` with no `passthrough` |
| the **renderer** | actually **reads** it: `item.content || renderChildren(item.body)` |

⇒ the one channel the renderer honours is the one the published faces refuse or drop, and the registration metadata is what recommends it.

## Why this is worth a card rather than a note

This is registration metadata — a key **stored by one author and re-authored by someone else**, including by AI writing metadata through the designer. An author who follows the registration's own guidance writes `items[].body`, the strict publish door strips it, and the list renders empty with nothing naming the dropped key. That is the shape where a declaration and its enforcement point opposite ways and the tooling coaches the losing side.

## What this card is NOT

⛔ Not a re-opening of objectui#9256's family-D ruling. That ruling is **node-level** — whether `ListSchema.body` / `.children` are read — and it was executed correctly: the node-level channels really are read by nothing, which is why they were tombstoned. **This defect is one level down, on `ListItem`**, where the channel IS live. The two do not conflict and neither supersedes the other.

## Suggested acceptance

- The three faces agree: either `items[].body` becomes declared on the published `ListItem` face and accepted by `ListItemSchema`, or the renderer stops reading it and the registration stops recommending it. ⛔ Not a silent strip on one side and a live read on the other.
- A pin that can go red: author a list item with `body` and no `content`, and assert the rendered output — shown failing before the repair.
- Whichever direction is chosen, the registration's authoring description moves with it in the same change.

## Measurement provenance

Surfaced by the objectui#9256 `list` + `timeline` slice while attributing all 473 `any`-receiver channel reads one by one — `list.tsx`'s `item.content || renderChildren(item.body)` was filed under `ListItem`, ⛔ not under `ListSchema`, which is exactly why the node-level sweep read `ListSchema` as reading neither channel while this item-level read stayed live. ⚠️ Re-derive before acting: line numbers and the exact description string are stale by default.

Refs: objectui#9256 · PR objectui#9589

Dedup terms for triage: `ListItem body` · `items[].body` · `ListItemSchema strips` · `list authoring input description` · `renderChildren(item.body)`
